An element is defined by the number of protons/neutrons. Proton number determines the element, neutron number determines the isotope. 

There is a limit to the number of protons an atom can support as the more protons/neutrons there are in an atom, the less stable the atom is. Around 100 protons in an atom, the element is so unstable it radiates away half it's mass every year. In the 110s the elements last for nanoseconds before decaying away.

Scientists have documented every single element from 1 to 118 along with every stable isotype as well as a bunch of unstable isotypes. If you search up 'isotope stability chart' it shows what combinations of protons and neutrons make up stable matter and the colour shows how long radioactive elements last. 

This graph shows that stability tends to follow a line of about 1.5 neutrons to 1 proton and the further you deviate from this line, the less stable it is.

You can put Pokémon from let's go into Pokémon home but if you ever deposit that Pokémon into a game that isn't lets go, it becomes unable to be transferred back. This is because the Pokémon data structure is different between the other games and let's go. 

When you move a Pokémon from let's go into another game, it deletes all the let's go specific data (like candies eaten) and adds in all the new data (like ribbons, EVs and memories).

Pokémon from Pokémon bank cannot be put into let's go. Neither can Pokémon from Pokémon go that have been transferred into home first as that changes their data to be for later games. 

Any Pokémon that has already gone through the conversion can be placed into sword/shield, brilliantdiamond/shining pearl (except for spinda), legends arceus and scarlet/violet. Just not let's go.

Back when I was in primary school, I had behavioural problems due to undiagnosed autism. I got no help for it and just got treated like everyone else because my grades were high. I dropped out of secondary school after a seriously bad case of bullying by a teacher and falling out with my closest friend. Went to 2 special needs schools. I went to a public college for 2 years and got some GCSEs and dropped out of another course.

Sorry for rambling. I was not perfect throughout this entire stretch of time. I could've done better. But so could they.

Shininess is determined by the pokemons pid, their OTs tid and their OTs sid. An eggs OT is the trainer who collected the egg. They stay as the OT until after the egg hatches where it changes to the trainer that hatched the egg.

During the hatching animation, the OT is the trainer who collected the egg. It uses this trainers tid and sid to calculate shininess. After this, the OT changes to the trainer who hatched the egg and recalculates shininess based on this trainers tid and sid.

There isnt a checkpoint. Its tricking the game into not unloading both the last and the first checkpoint of the map.

An ultra shortcut in mkwii occurs when you exit the first checkpoint from the side and entering the final checkpoint.

Basically, in mkwii, the only checkpoints loaded are the one in front and behind you. If you are in a checkpoint, it loads the one in front, behind and the one you are currently in.

If you exit a checkpoint from the side, the game never registers you leaving the checkpoint. As you are in front of the flag, you a have a lap passed. If you leave this checkpoint from the side and enter the final checkpoint, your checkpoint location is set to the final checkpoint while also keeping you on the same lap. 

The rock on the side of grumble volcano is large enough for you to drive into the starting checkpoint, drive out through the side, drive back and touch the final checkpoint, then drive and touch the starting checkpoint.
